about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Stephanie I. Bice

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GPO MODERNIZATION ACT OF 2026
statements.title: GPO MODERNIZATION ACT OF 2026
sentences: I rise today in strong support of H.R. 9342, the GPO Modernization Act of 2026.
Mr. Speaker, I thank GPO Director Halpern and the CHA staff for their work on this, and I urge my colleagues to join me in supporting this bipartisan commonsense legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WAIVING A REQUIREMENT OF CLAUSE 6(a) OF RULE XIII WITH RESPECT TO CONSIDERATION OF CERTAIN RESOLUTIONS REPORTED FROM THE COMMITTEE ON RULES
statements.title: WAIVING A REQUIREMENT OF CLAUSE 6(a) OF RULE XIII WITH RESPECT TO CONSIDERATION OF CERTAIN RESOLUTIONS REPORTED FROM THE COMMITTEE ON RULES
sentences: Thankfully, President Trump used emergency measures to ensure that the Coast Guard, Border Patrol, TSA, and others received pay, but Democrats proved they were more than willing to hold more than 260,000 employees who work at DHS hostage.
While most of the agency was funded in May, additional resources for Customs and Border Protection and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement are still needed.
The difference couldn't be more clear: Under the Biden administration, more than 10 million illegals crossed the southern border.
During the last year, there have been zero releases at the border, and apprehensions in April were 94 percent lower than the monthly average under the previous administration.
Under my friend and fellow Oklahoman, Secretary Markwayne Mullin, I know the Department will continue to ensure our border is closed, ultimately protecting our homeland.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of the rule to allow for consideration of the Senate's forthcoming reconciliation bill.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all of my colleagues to support this rule.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: INCREASE IN RETIREMENT AGE OF UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE OFFICERS
statements.title: INCREASE IN RETIREMENT AGE OF UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE OFFICERS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill (H.R. 8364) to amend title 5, United States Code, to authorize the increase of the retirement age in the United States Capitol Police.
I rise today in support of Bryan Steil's legislation, H.R. 8364, which extends the retirement waiver age for officers within the United States Capitol Police.
Although we have seen a welcome and much-needed increase in recruitment numbers, we continue to have staffing challenges within the United States Capitol Police.
Under current law, officers are forced to retire at age 57, unless they receive a waiver from the Capitol Police Board.
Under our legislation, the Capitol Police Board will have the authority to grant waivers to sworn officers until they reach the age of 65.
In 2004 and 2010, Congress temporarily raised the mandatory Federal law enforcement retirement age from 60 to 65 to address staffing shortfalls at the FBI.
Additionally, it is also important to note that our legislation gives the Capitol Police Board the discretion to decide who is still fit for the job.
The men and women of the U.S. Capitol Police do a tremendous job protecting this institution.
Again, I thank the ranking member and his staff for working closely with us on this important matter, and I urge my colleagues to support the legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SEMIQUINCENTENNIAL CONGRESSIONAL TIME CAPSULE ACT
statements.title: SEMIQUINCENTENNIAL CONGRESSIONAL TIME CAPSULE ACT
sentences: Madam Speaker, today I urge my colleagues to support S. 3705, the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule Act.

statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 7148, CONSOLIDATED APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; AND PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 7147, DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; AND FOR...

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of the rule to consider the final four fiscal year 2026 appropriations bills.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONSOLIDATED APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026
statements.title: CONSOLIDATED APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026
sentences: It invests in transportation infrastructure and housing affordability while cutting wasteful spending and reducing the Federal bureaucracy.

The package supports housing affordability and community development by providing $3.3 billion for the Community Development Block Grants and $1.25 billion for the HOME program, giving States and localities flexible tools to expand affordable housing.
It also eliminates waste, including $929 million from the failed California High-Speed Rail project, which has been totally mismanaged and is completely indefensible.
Nearly $1 billion in Biden-era Green New Deal spending is redirected to critical infrastructure needs.
Mr. Chair, I rise in strong support of H.R. 7148, which contains the Defense, Labor-Health and Human Services-Education, and Transportation-Housing and Urban Development appropriations bills.
Mr. Chair, I urge passage of this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: UNLOCKING OUR DOMESTIC LNG POTENTIAL ACT OF 2025
statements.title: UNLOCKING OUR DOMESTIC LNG POTENTIAL ACT OF 2025
sentences: A recent S&P Global study found that U.S. LNG exports reduce global greenhouse gas emissions by 65 million tons.
Anyone serious about lowering global emissions should strongly support the expansion of American LNG.

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of the Unlocking Our Domestic LNG Potential Act, which will support a robust natural gas industry in the U.S. and meet President Trump's goal of achieving American energy dominance.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to join me in voting in favor of this legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STOP ILLEGAL ENTRY ACT OF 2025
statements.title: STOP ILLEGAL ENTRY ACT OF 2025
sentences: Under the Biden administration, over 10 million illegal immigrants entered this country.
Customs and Border Patrol caught 400 individuals on the terrorist watch list, leaving us the question of who else was allowed to enter this country undetected.
The legislation seeks to discourage migrants from coming to the U.S. illegally and keeps criminal aliens who disregard Federal immigration law out of our American communities.

It is vital that law enforcement officers and Border Patrol officers have the tools they need to hold dangerous criminals accountable and safeguard our communities, and this legislation does just that.
President Trump has delivered on his promise to secure the border, and this legislation provides the tools needed to uphold our laws and remove dangerous criminals.
As a former prosecutor, I know he understands the importance of strong policies that safeguard our communities and empower law enforcement.

The previous administration allowed an unprecedented invasion of illegal immigration, resulting in the influx of limitless criminal aliens--including murderers, rapists, child traffickers and smugglers, drug dealers, and more--entering the United States and further enriching foreign terrorist cartels.
President Trump took immediate action to seal and secure the border.

Now, to ensure long term border security and deter the most heinous illegal criminal aliens from attempting to re-enter the United States, there must be stronger criminal penalties to prevent illegal re-entry following removal.
For example, an off-duty Customs and Border Patrol officer was shot in the face in New York City in July by an illegal alien who was deported and reentered under the previous administration.

Last December, a Guatemalan illegal alien, who was previously deported under the first Trump Administration and later illegally re- entered, was indicted for lighting a woman on fire and burning her to death on a New York City subway.

Additionally, H.R. 3486 cracks down on the smuggling of illicit drugs across the border, often through cartel organizations, by imposing the possibility of up to fifteen years in prison for illegal aliens convicted of three or more misdemeanors involving drugs or harm against others, or for illegal aliens who attempt to reenter after being removed three times.
Madam Speaker, I rise today in support of my legislation, H.R. 3486, the Stop Illegal Entry Act.
Madam Speaker, I urge the passage of this important legislation to hold those accountable that are here illegally.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THANKING POLICE OFFICERS FOR ALL THEY DO
statements.title: THANKING POLICE OFFICERS FOR ALL THEY DO
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in honor of National Police Week, which serves as a reminder to remember and memorialize law enforcement officers who have fallen in the line of duty.

During this week, I am reminded of a quote from Matthew chapter 5, verse 9: ``Blessed are the peacekeepers, for they shall be called the children of God.'' Our law enforcement officers put themselves in harm's way every day in the pursuit of justice and protection of the innocent.
One of the greatest strengths of law enforcement is their ability to bridge gaps, forge connections, and build trust within our communities.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT
statements.title: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, or the SAVE Act.
Mr. Speaker, under President Biden, nearly 5 million illegal aliens were released into the United States.
Biden's failure at the southern border has diluted the voting power that is reserved for only American citizens.
The SAVE Act will strengthen our election administration, improve voter confidence, and ensure that American elections are only for American citizens.
Specifically, it amends the National Voter Registration Act to require States to obtain proof of citizenship when an individual registers to vote.
This is already required when you update your ID, your Social Security records, and, yes, your voter registration, too.
REAL IDs, passports, and other valid forms of ID mentioned in the SAVE Act are sufficient proof of citizenship.

I will add this: The claim is that it will disenfranchise married women and others who might have to change their names because the documentation might show two different names, but the SAVE Act itself addresses this point in the text.
Mr. Speaker, I strongly support the SAVE Act, and I look forward to voting for it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REPEAL REQUIREMENT FOR CONGRESSIONAL RESEARCH SERVICE TO PREPARE ANNOTATED CONSTITUTION AND SUPPLEMENTS IN HARDBOUND VERSION
statements.title: REPEAL REQUIREMENT FOR CONGRESSIONAL RESEARCH SERVICE TO PREPARE ANNOTATED CONSTITUTION AND SUPPLEMENTS IN HARDBOUND VERSION
sentences: These copies were eventually expanded to include Supreme Court case citations so that Members could see which clauses of the Constitution the Court used in deciding cases.

The Constitution provides the framework for our government, and understanding that framework and how the Supreme Court has applied it to its decisions over the years is as essential today as it was 200 years ago.
Today, most of us rely on digital sources for the most up-to-date information, whether it is news, airfares, the weather, or Supreme Court case citations.
The site is publicly accessible, easy to search, provides links to Supreme Court decisions, and, perhaps most importantly, is updated in real time by the CRS.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to join me in supporting H.R. 1234.

statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY RELATING TO "ENERGY CONSERVATION PROGRAM: ENERGY CONSERVATION STANDARDS FOR WALK-IN COOLERS AND WALK-IN...

By doing so, we will protect small businesses from unnecessary compliance costs and preserve the diversity of choice available to consumers.
I urge my colleagues to support H.J. Res. 24, legislation that will reduce burdens on businesses and serve the best interests of the American people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FULL-YEAR CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2025
statements.title: FULL-YEAR CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2025
sentences: They keep talking about impacts to mandatory spending, Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

We must keep government open so we can continue the America First agenda, which is focused on securing our border, unleashing American energy, safeguarding our Nation, and rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse.
Continuing resolutions are not ideal, but we cannot allow for the distractions of a government shutdown, which is why I support this bill.
I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes.''

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING AMERICAN ENERGY PRODUCTION ACT
statements.title: PROTECTING AMERICAN ENERGY PRODUCTION ACT
sentences: According to the America First Policy Institute, hydraulic fracturing saves Americans $203 billion annually in reduced energy costs.
It is also important to remember that the argument against updated drilling technology is built on misinformation.

Under the Obama administration, the EPA found that hydraulic fracturing has no widespread systemic impacts on resources in the U.S. Modern drilling technology techniques are safe, effective, and crucial to maintaining our energy independence.
Madam Speaker, I am proud to support H.R. 26, the Protecting American Energy Production Act.
Madam Speaker, I urge my colleagues to join me in supporting H.R. 26, and I thank Mr. Pfluger for bringing this forward.
